summary: The port opens with roughly the right plum/blue amoeba look but stops animating after ~1-2 s and fades to near-black, while the original churns continuously and holds steady brightness indefinitely.
observations: Rig for both sides: strip, 60 px, seed 1, same clock; neither side reported a compile or runtime error in any run.

Original (6 s waterfall, baseline): a magenta/plum field with ~4-6 soft-edged blue blobs 8-15 px wide that drift and deform laterally, punctuated by black voids ~5-10 px wide lasting ~0.3-0.6 s each; edges are smooth gradients.

Port (same 6 s window): the same plum/blue/black color family and a similar feature scale for roughly the first 0.5-1 s, but the waterfall is then made of straight vertical streaks, i.e. every pixel holds its value — the field is frozen.

Numerically: original meanBrightness stays 43-58 across all 120 frames with motion 1-17 (avg 3, only 2 zero frames). Port meanBrightness decays 42 -> 13 by frame 47 (2.35 s), sits flat at 12-13, then drops to 3 by frame 119; motion is exactly 0 for 82 of 120 frames and never exceeds 4.

30 s window (--seconds 30 --fps 4): original is unchanged in character at t=30 s (mean 44, motion avg 13 at 0.25 s spacing) — continuously churning blue blobs on plum. Port is black over almost the whole image (mean 7, and that is dominated by the first ~2 s), with only a couple of surviving lit pixel columns at the frame edges.

Warm-up is not the explanation and it does not recover: --skip 20 (capturing t=20-26 s) gives original mean 49 / motion 4 and a full, lively blob field, while the port is mean 2 / motion 0 and visually solid black except one faint blue column at the left edge.
Not a one-seed fluke: seed 9 shows the same thing (orig mean 49, motion avg 3, 2 zero-motion frames; port mean 12, motion avg 1, 81/120 zero-motion frames, ending at brightness 2).

Not a rig artifact: on an 8x8 grid rig (2 s contact sheet) both sides show plum backgrounds with blue bands and dark voids, and the port is still recognizable there because the freeze has not fully set in yet — but even in those 2 s the port averages mean 29 vs the original's 48, and its features have hard, blocky, quantized edges where the original's are smooth gradients. A 16x13 grid gives identical numbers.

Color family matches on both sides: meanG is exactly 0 in every frame of every run, with red and blue channels only (original avg R 49 / B 95; port avg R 12 / B 40 over 6 s, i.e. same hue family, ~3x dimmer and getting dimmer).
feedback: The dominant bug: the port's field stops evolving. Frame-to-frame motion falls to exactly 0 by ~2 s and stays there for the rest of a 30 s capture, whereas the original never has two consecutive still frames. Whatever advances the pattern (its time/animation driver) is running once or converging instead of running continuously — fix this before anything else, since it makes the pattern invisible in normal use.

Second bug, probably the same root cause: the port's overall brightness decays monotonically instead of holding. Original meanBrightness stays in a 43-58 band forever; the port goes 42 -> 13 in 2.3 s -> 3 at 6 s -> 2 at 20 s. The target is a steady-state mean around 45-50 with no long-term downward trend.

Target motion statistics once it is animating: at 20 fps the original's mean abs frame-diff sits around 2-4 with periodic spikes to 8-17 (blobs being born/dying). The port should land in that range rather than 0-1.

Structure/edge quality: the original's blobs and voids are smooth gradients — a blue blob ramps into the plum background over several pixels. The port's features have hard, blocky, step-like edges (clearly visible in both the strip waterfall and the 8x8 grid sheet). Soften the spatial falloff so features read as blobs, not rectangles.

Color is the one axis that already matches and should be preserved: plum/magenta background, pure blue highlights, black voids, green channel at zero throughout. Do not change the palette while fixing the motion.

Feature scale in the original, for calibration on a 60 px strip: roughly 4-6 blue blobs on screen at once, each 8-15 px wide, plus black voids 5-10 px wide that appear and vanish on a ~0.3-0.6 s timescale; lateral drift is slow (a blob shifts only a few pixels per second, so the waterfall streaks are near-vertical but visibly wandering).
